newsitem.title: PORTUGAL: Spain, Portugal to pledge to join first EMU group.
newsitem.headline: Spain, Portugal to pledge to join first EMU group.

text.p: The prime ministers of Spain and Portugal are expected to pledge later on Wednesday to join a single European currency from the start, officials said.

Spanish Prime Minister Jose Maria Aznar and his Portuguese counterpart, Antonio Guterres, discussed their countries' ambitions to join the first wave of nations taking part in the euro currency on Tuesday night.
They ruled out any delay in the timetable under which the euro is due to be launched in January 1999, the officials said.
Aznar and Guterres wind up a two-day meeting in the Azores on Wednesday.

The single currency dominated talks between officials of the two countries, which also ranged from bilateral issues such as scarce water resources to international matters, including the European Union summit in Dublin in December.

"Portugal and Spain do not wish to be treated as peripheral countries in matters relating to the single currency," Portuguese Economy Minister Augusto Mateus told reporters after meeting his Spanish counterpart, Rodrigo Rato.
"They want to be at the centre of the political debate at a European level. Portugal and Spain are against any delay in the timetable set for the European single currency."
Officials said their countries were on target to meet the tough economic criteria for joining the single currency.
"Each country has evaluated its performance and the conclusion is positive. We (Portugal) have the right conditions to join the founding group of the single currency," Mateus said.
Spanish officials expressed support for Portugal's efforts to win self-determination for the people of the former Portuguese colony of East Timor.
"Spain has supported Portugal in its campaign in favour of Timor and this was reaffirmed again here," a Portuguese government source said.

Portuguese President Jorge Sampaio said this week he would accept an offer to head a Lisbon-based foundation supporting East Timor's independence cause, which is to be created by Nobel laureate Jose Ramos-Horta.

East Timor has been in turmoil since Indonesia invaded it in 1975. The United Nations does not recognise Indonesian sovereignty and considers Portugal, the former colonial power, as the administering power.
Spanish and Portuguese officials were expected on Wednesday to discuss judicial and police coooperation in the war on terrorism and drug trafficking.
"We will discuss the fight against drug addiction, drug trafficking, the traffic in women and money laundering," Portuguese Justice Minister Jose Vera Jardim said.
The police forces of Spain and Portugal are struggling to contain increasingly powerful and innovative drug gangs which run cocaine, heroin and cannabis into the countries by land and sea.
Portugal congratulated Spain on the appointment of Spaniard Miguel Angel Moratinos as the EU's special envoy to the Middle East, officials added.
